newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes hover at new peak after buying spree.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes hover at new peak after buying spree.

text.p: The North Sea crude market held steady on Friday, pausing for breath at the peak of recent gains.
Dated Brent traded twice at August Brent +17 cents, unchanged from a deal done on Thursday.
The French refiner which bought an August 8-10 cargo also sold a 6-8, keeping its tally of August Brents at five.
The buyer of the 8-10 cargo was a U.S. refiner which has booked a vessel to take two million barrels of Brent to the U.S. Gulf in early August, but has had little luck finding buyers.
Two more Brent cargoes were due to be nominated loading dates on Friday.
Traders said that a flurry of buying of first-half August North Sea cargoes helped firm the market.
As many as half a dozen Ekofisks were heard sold on Thursday with premiums to Dated Brent in the high 20s.
"We've seen a lot of short-covering into the second decade, but it looks like the market has peaked...buyers are quite relaxed and sellers are not that aggressive," said one trader.

With Iraqi exports not expected until mid-August at the earliest, refiners had to cover their requirements, but few were willing to pay much higher numbers with Iraqi flows likely to be in excess of 1.5 million barrels per day when they do resume.
Brent CFDs and intermonth spreads were also strong. August/September traded at +18 cents in the U.S. aftermarket, while Sep/Oct notched up a cent to trade at -4 cents on Friday.
CFDs for next week (July 28-Aug 01) were bid about three cents higher at September Brent +10 cents and later weeks were also slightly firmer.
September Brent was trading eight cents down at $18.36 a barrel on the IPE screen at 1210 GMT, having traded at $18.35 on the paper market.
